description: For analysts and the people who rely on their numbers: define a metric once so everyone gets the same figure, review SQL for the bugs that quietly inflate it, and spec dashboards around a decision instead of every chart that was easy to make.

prerequisites: A SQL query whose number you need to trust, and the database it runs on
first-value.starter-task: Check a query before its number goes into a report
first-value.starter-prompt:
Review this Postgres query before it goes into the finance dashboard. One row per region; customers.customer_id is unique and an order has many order_items. Finance reports in New York time.

SELECT c.region, SUM(o.amount_usd) AS revenue_usd
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.created_at BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY c.region;
first-value.verification: sql-review opens with a verdict, flags the order_items join as multiplying revenue and the BETWEEN as losing 30 September, gives a corrected query with New York boundaries, and lists verification queries to prove the fix.
first-value.recovery: If the review jumps to indexes before correctness, ask for it by name ("use sql-review"). If it guesses the database, tell it which one: integer division and timezone functions differ between engines.

journey.when: A number matters (a board metric, a finance figure, a team KPI) and people either disagree about it or are about to build a dashboard on it.
you_bring: the metric name and the question it answers
the tables it comes from, and any SQL or dashboard already computing it
who reads it and what they decide

steps.you_do: Give it the metric, the sources, and any existing SQL.
steps.you_get: One written definition: exact formula, grain, window and timezone, exclusions with predicates, allowed dimensions, edge cases, owner, reference SQL and sanity checks.
steps.decide: Confirm the open decisions (timezone, exclusions, lock period) with the metric's owner.

steps.you_do: Run it on the definition's reference SQL, or on any query that already reports the number.
steps.you_get: A verdict and line-by-line findings, each with the wrong result and corrected SQL, plus the full corrected query and verification queries.
steps.decide: Certify the metric, or fix the SQL and review again.

steps.you_do: Give it the audience, the decision and the list of requested charts.
steps.you_get: A one-page spec: questions in priority order, one chart per question built on your defined metrics, filters, freshness SLA, layout, and a cut list.

steps.you_do: Run it on the metric spec or dashboard spec before sharing it with the BI team.
steps.you_get: A verdict and severity-tagged findings with a fix for each.
steps.decide: Hand the spec to the builder, or revise it.

journey.you_end_with: A certified metric definition with reviewed reference SQL, and a dashboard spec a BI developer can build without guessing.
